Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

PortinariColors 0.3.0

  • Palettes now have a style, as in RColorBrewer and MetBrewer: qualitative (cafe, paz), diverging (retirantes, inah, sofia, guerra) and sequential (guerra_azul, paz_ouro). portinari.palettes() and show_portinari() gain a category filter.
  • New sequential palettes guerra_azul and paz_ouro, derived from the UN panels.
  • Palettes are stored MetBrewer-style: colors in display order plus an order ranking for discrete picks. Discrete subsets now suit the style: sequential and diverging palettes keep both ends (and the light centre), qualitative palettes keep the most distinct colors. The colors returned for a given n have changed for every palette.
  • sofia is now colorblind-safe for its first 3 colors (was 2).
  • New portinari.works() lists the paintings behind each palette with links.
  • Hex logo: a portrait of Portinari in the light shades of guerra.
  • pkgdown site with two articles: “The paintings” (images and links for every reference work) and “Choosing a palette style”.

PortinariColors 0.2.0

  • New palettes guerra (9 colors, all colorblind-safe) and paz (8 colors, first 4 colorblind-safe), from Portinari’s Guerra and Paz panels at the United Nations Headquarters.
  • Continuous palettes and scales now interpolate along a smooth ramp order stored with each palette, instead of the discrete priority order. Gradients for every palette are smoother as a result.

PortinariColors 0.1.0

  • First release: portinari.pal(), scale_color_portinari(), scale_colour_portinari(), scale_fill_portinari(), portinari.palettes(), portinari.cvd.check() and show_portinari().
  • Four palettes: cafe, retirantes, inah, sofia. Two are colorblind-safe for all colors, two for a subset.
